findings.title: test_data_sink_impl fails to compile at SEASTAR_API_LEVEL 7/8
findings.claim: test_data_sink_impl only implements the SEASTAR_API_LEVEL >= 9 put(std::span<...>) overload; at API levels 7/8 (which CMakeLists.txt:72 and configure.py --api-level support) data_sink_impl::put(net::packet) remains pure virtual, so the class is abstract and the override refers to nothing, causing a hard compile error. This would only affect non-default builds since CI only builds the default API level.

findings.title: stream_close() now defers stop()/abort()/shutdown_input() behind outgoing-queue drain, allowing hangs
findings.claim: Previously write_buf.close() returned promptly even with a write in flight and the immediate stop() eventually caused stop_send_loop() to call shutdown_output() and break a stalled send; now, with stop() deferred, a send stalled on a full send window (e.g. a compressor empty frame with the peer no longer draining) leaves sink.close()/the source read hung until the connection is aborted from outside.

findings.title: _outgoing_queue_ready becomes a ready future while entries can still be linked in _outgoing_queue, breaking its tail-entry invariant
findings.claim: The change leaves _outgoing_queue_ready as a ready future even though entries can still be linked into _outgoing_queue, breaking the invariant that it should be the tail entry's done future; the report notes nothing enqueues after that point today (send() is refused, enqueue_zero_frame() only runs from the client ctor), but a future enqueue path that misses the _stream_closing check would fire immediately and re-open the race this PR fixes.
